item.title: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
item.description:
Fiona, the beloved Cincinnati Zoo hippo who became a global sensation after surviving a premature birth nearly a decade ago, has died after swallowing a visitor’s knit hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure, the zoo announced Thursday. The 9-year-old hippo died from complications after veterinarians and animal-care staff made multiple attempts to save her, according to the Associated Press. About 11 days ago, a visitor tossed the knit hat into the air, but a ceiling fan caught it and flung it through a small opening above the enclosure’s viewing windows. “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement. This is a developing story.

item.title: Rohingya genocide survivor: ‘perpetrators will have to face consequences’
item.description:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "far-reaching implications in future genocide cases," including South Africa's case against Israel over Gaza. Brody also discusses the Gambia's role in bringing the case and growing challenges to international accountability, warning that "we're in a very dangerous moment."
